newsitem.title: USA: Viacom opens first entertainment store.
newsitem.headline: Viacom opens first entertainment store.

text.p: Entertainment giant Viacom Inc. unveiled a theme store here on Thursday, the first of several retail outlets that the company hopes will bolster revenue by exploiting its Nickelodeon, Star Trek and MTV brands names.

The Viacom Entertainment Store, a playhouse of products designed after Viacom's cable TV characters and Hollywood studio hits, is as much an effort to build revenue as to heighten recognition of its obscure corporate name.
"Viacom is not a household name," said Chairman and Chief Executive Sumner Redstone during a press conference at the new store along the posh Michigan Avenue retailing district here.
"We think the store will help change that," he added.
The company plans to open a total of four to five "Viacom" entertainment outlets in the United States during the next several years, he said.
New York, San Francisco, Las Vegas and Boston are other cities the company's retailing division could target for stores because of their large size and tourist following, Redstone said.

The Chicago store is scheduled to open Friday after a celebrity-studded party Thursday evening with a performance by the band Jon Bon Jovi. The shop will sell 2,500 products displayed around huge props and sets fashioned after Viacom's MTV and Nick at Nite TV programming, and the movie Star Trek.
Viacom's retail arm also plans to open five Nickelodeon-themed boutiques in shopping malls by the fourth quarter, Redstone said.
"The big economic play is going to be the boutique stores as we roll them out to the best malls in America," he said.
In addition to those boutiques, other shops modelled around Star Trek and MTV are possible down the road, he added.

Viacom is coming into a market already dominated by Walt Disney Co., which has 429 Disney stores, and Time Warner's 161 Warner Bros. stores. But the company claims the Viacom entertainment stores will differ from their competitors by offering products that appeal to a lot of different ages.
"Success is more important than speed," Redstone said. "No matter how crowded the field is, there's always room for a winner."
Viacom's stock rose 9.38 cents to $29.28 on the American Stock Exchange.
